before:
Mastering: States that displacement only occurs when the added halogen is more reactive than the halogen in solution; explains that chlorine is more reactive than bromine because chlorine’s outer shell is closer to the nucleus (less shielded), so it attracts an incoming electron more strongly; concludes that bromine is therefore unable to displace the less reactive bromide ions from chloride ions — correction: bromine is less reactive than chlorine and cannot take electrons away from chloride ions.
Secure: Correct statement that bromine is less reactive than chlorine with an explanation in terms of electron structure.
Developing: States bromine is less reactive without the electron-structure explanation.
Emerging: Vague or incorrect explanation.
